name: Kashi Art Cafe
signature_dish: Chocolate cake and filter-style coffee in a restored Dutch row house
why_it_matters: Opened 1997 inside a restored Dutch-era row house off Burgher Street, Kashi paired a contemporary art gallery with a cafe years before Fort Kochi became a biennale town — it is effectively the original of the Fort Kochi cafe scene. The garden-courtyard tables and rotating gallery shows make it the address every Fort Kochi walking tour passes through.
insider_tip: Go for breakfast before 10am to beat the cruise-ship crowd; the small back courtyard is cooler than the front room. The chocolate cake sells out by mid-afternoon. Cash + cards + UPI accepted.
signature_address: House No 1/554, Burgher Street, opp. St. Mary's Anglo Indian Girls High School, Fort Kochi, Kochi, Kerala 682001

name: History at Brunton Boatyard
signature_dish: Seafood thali tracing Fort Kochi's Portuguese, Dutch, British, Arab and Jewish kitchens
why_it_matters: The signature restaurant of CGH Earth's Brunton Boatyard — a heritage hotel built on a restored Victorian shipyard on Cochin Harbour. The menu is a deliberate culinary history of Fort Kochi: Portuguese, Dutch, British Raj, Arab, Jewish (kosher) and local Malayali dishes researched from community recipes. The harbour-facing terrace looks straight onto the Vypeen ferry channel.
insider_tip: Book a harbour-side table for sunset and ask for the seafood thali — it changes with the day's catch and is the most complete way to taste the menu's range. Non-residents are welcome but should reserve, especially in the Dec-Feb season.
signature_address: Brunton Boatyard, Calvathy Road, Fort Kochi, Kochi, Kerala 682001

name: Kayees Rahmathulla Cafe
signature_dish: Kayikka's mutton biryani — the dum biryani Kochi locals call an emotion
why_it_matters: Founded 1948 by V.K. Kayee — 'Kaikka' — an ex-British Army cook who started a Mattancherry tea shop and turned it into a restaurant by 1951. 'Kayikkante biryani' is a Kochi institution; the Mattancherry flagship is the reference branch and the dish has its own Wikipedia entry. Locals queue here for a plate the way they would for a festival meal.
insider_tip: Biryani is cooked in batches and sells out — go by 1pm for lunch or you'll be told to wait for the next dum. The Mattancherry original is the one to visit, not the newer city outlets. Cash and UPI; small, no-frills room.
signature_address: Kayees Junction, Pullupalam Road, New Road, Mattancherry, Kochi, Kerala 682002

name: Fusion Bay
area: KB Jacob Road, Santa Cruz Basilica Junction, Fort Kochi
signature_dish: Fish pollichathu — sea bass marinated and grilled in banana leaf
why_it_matters: A family-run Fort Kochi seafood room near Santa Cruz Basilica, Fusion Bay is the locals' alternative to the tourist-priced waterfront places — 4.4 on TripAdvisor across nearly 4,000 reviews. The kitchen leans Kerala Syrian-Christian: pollichathu, mango fish curry and Malabar-spiced prawns, with the catch adjusted daily.
insider_tip: Small room, opens 1pm — expect a short wait at dinner; staff will dial spice down on request. No alcohol. Cost for two runs around ₹700, far below the harbour-view restaurants nearby.
signature_address: 1/568, KB Jacob Road, Santa Cruz Basilica Junction, Fort Kochi, Kochi, Kerala 682001

name: Dhe Puttu
signature_dish: Puttu in dozens of variations — from classic rice-and-coconut to erachi (beef) and chocolate puttu
why_it_matters: A themed restaurant near Lulu Mall in Edappally dedicated entirely to puttu — Kerala's steamed rice-cylinder breakfast staple — co-owned by Malayalam film stars Dileep and Nadirshah. The kitchen serves 30-plus variations under one roof, from traditional kadala-puttu to chocolate and Schezwan puttu, with a model goods train delivering plates. One of Ernakulam's busiest restaurants.
insider_tip: Come for an early dinner — it fills up after 7.30pm. First-timers should order the classic puttu-kadala combo before experimenting with the novelty versions; the beef puttu is the standout. Cards and UPI accepted.
signature_address: NH 66 Bypass, near Lulu Mall, Edappally, Ernakulam, Kochi, Kerala 682024

name: Indian Coffee House
signature_dish: Filter coffee, masala dosa and mutton cutlet served by the turbaned cooperative waiters
why_it_matters: Part of the worker-cooperative Indian Coffee House movement — the Thrissur-headquartered society was incorporated in 1958 and runs 50-plus Kerala branches. The Ernakulam outlets are everyday institutions: cheap, unchanging, run by the staff themselves, with the recognisable turbaned uniform and a menu that has barely moved in decades.
insider_tip: Order the mutton cutlet with filter coffee — the cutlet is the dish ICH regulars come for. It is a cooperative, so service is unhurried; this is a place to sit, not rush. Cash only at most branches.
signature_address: Indian Coffee House, Durbar Hall Road, Ernakulam, Kochi, Kerala 682016

name: Pandhal
signature_dish: Plum cake and Kerala-style bakery snacks alongside a full meals menu
why_it_matters: A long-standing MG Road bakery-restaurant brand in central Ernakulam — the kind of place locals stop at for tea-time puffs, cutlets and bakery boxes, and for an everyday Kerala lunch. The cake shop is a fixture of Ernakulam's MG Road and the brand has since spread to David Hall (Fort Kochi) and Kadavanthra outlets.
insider_tip: Best treated as a bakery-and-snacks stop rather than a destination dinner — the puffs and cutlets are fresh in the late afternoon. The MG Road branch is the original; the David Hall Fort Kochi outlet is the heritage-courtyard one.
signature_address: Pandhal, MG Road, Ernakulam, Kochi, Kerala 682011

name: Hotel Seagull
signature_dish: Kerala-style fish curry and grilled prawns on a harbour-facing terrace
why_it_matters: A waterfront restaurant-and-bar on Calvathy Road overlooking the Fort Kochi shipping channel — one of the few Fort Kochi spots where you can watch cargo ships pass while eating fresh Kerala seafood. A reliable, long-running choice for an unfussy sundowner-and-seafood evening on the harbour.
insider_tip: Go for the terrace tables at sunset; the channel-side seats fill first. It serves alcohol, unlike many Fort Kochi seafood rooms — handy if you want a beer with the crab roast.
signature_address: Hotel Seagull, Calvathy Road, Fort Kochi, Kochi, Kerala 682001
